oracle.ref: PR #1100 (fix); fix evidence: dskeepem 10/10/2026 (stand from 96a53b266): page.look reported padding 'set: padding: var(--ds-btn-pad-y,15px) var(--ds-btn-pad-x,30px), by: .btn-primary @layer components' before and after the write while computed 19px 38px came from `!px-[calc(…)]`/`!py-[calc(…)]` (padding-inline/padding-block !important, @layer utilities) — tasks/evidence/followups-2026-10-10/p2-look/em-page-look-padding-*.json.
oracle.invariant: S1 exits 0. padding names the utilities, not .btn-primary: parts top/bottom by the !py rule (padding-block … !important) and right/left by the !px rule (padding-inline … !important), layer 'utilities'; padding-left, padding-inline and padding-block-start read the same rules; rtl maps padding-inline-start to padding-right, vertical-rl maps padding-block-start to padding-right. Among !important declarations the earliest layer wins (.c0.c0 @layer base over @layer utilities and over an unlayered #t.c1), a layered one beats an unlayered one, the style attribute beats both; normal declarations keep the browser's order (the unlayered rule wins). look.set against a !important utility in @layer utilities writes its rule inside '@layer utilities { … !important }'; sides held !important by two different layers are refused, nothing written.
